text.brief: In February 1968 Party security arrested Sidney Rittenberg, an American Party member who had worked for its broadcasters, and put him in solitary confinement.
text.record: Rittenberg came to China as an Army linguist in 1945 and stayed to serve the Party. The Party had already imprisoned him from 1949 to 1955 on a false spy charge, and it held him again from 1968 to 1977. He left for the United States in 1980 and later advised American firms on business in China.
text.reading: The Party consumes its allies as readily as its enemies, and a foreigner's loyalty buys no exemption. Rittenberg's decades of service ended in sixteen years of prison, the Consume stage applied to a true believer.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. No government could reach an American held by a state with which the United States had no relations.
text.fix: Keep consular channels open even with adversaries, because the absence of relations leaves citizens with no advocate.
